op.ts.title: Transition state
op.ts.does: Finds a minimum-energy path between two structures, its TS(s), and (by default) optimizes each TS and follows its IRC. Multi-step paths are split into elementary steps, adding intermediates.
how: Snapshots both geometries into the job folder and runs `mepd run --start --end` with the job's profile as --inputs (operations._build_ts).
Minimizes endpoints not yet minima at this level (engine geometry optimization, up to 500 cycles), then SLAPMapper checks and, if on, fixes the atom correspondence.
Builds the initial path (the profile's interpolation, default geodesic, 10 images) and relaxes it with the profile's path method (default NEB).
Recursive: MSMEP checks each path for intermediate minima and pseudo-IRC endpoints and splits it into new searches (msmep.MSMEP.run_recursive_minimize).
TS optimization from each leaf's highest image, then IRC; for g-xTB both through ASE/Sella (cli_common._optimize_ts_and_irc).
op.ts.default: Recursive splitting, TS optimization and IRC on, atom-mapping check on: a path with an intermediate otherwise gives one meaningless TS guess.

swap.option: Single path minimization or parallel branches
Path method (NEB, FNEB, FSM-TS, GSM, MLPGI, NEB-DLF, geomeTRIC NEB)

swap.where: Settings › profile (Compute profile in this form)

caveats: The TS found is the one nearest these two conformers; a lower channel may exist (use Reaction channels).
A failed TS optimization is a warning: the path result still stands.

param.ts.path_mode.title: Path search
param.ts.path_mode.does: Chooses between one path minimization and recursive splitting of multi-step paths into elementary steps.
how: single: the profile's path minimizer runs once on the initial path (cli._build_path_minimizer); the highest image is the TS guess.

recursive (--recursive): after each minimization, check_if_elem_step minimizes interior minima and runs a pseudo-IRC from the peak; if new minima appear, the path is split there and each leg searched again (MSMEP).
parallel (--parallel): the same, with split branches run concurrently (threads; processes for local QCCompute), up to min(4, CPUs) unless Parallel workers is set.
param.ts.path_mode.default: recursive: the most reliable way to get elementary steps with verifiable TSs.
caveats: Network completion with 'single' still turns on recursive splitting.

param.ts.use_tsopt.title: Optimize TS
param.ts.use_tsopt.does: Refines each path's highest-energy image to a first-order saddle point, written as ts*.xyz.
how: Takes each leaf's highest-energy image (QM/MM: the interpolated maximum plus the path tangent) as the guess (cli._ts_guess).
Calls engine.compute_transition_state: for g-xTB and ASE engines Sella with order=1, fmax 0.01 eV/Å, up to 500 steps; for QCCompute engines geomeTRIC's transition_state run.
A failed optimization is reported and skipped; the path stays.
param.ts.use_tsopt.default: On: path images are only TS guesses.

swap.where: not exposed: engine.compute_transition_state in mepd/engines/*.py (ASEEngine.transition_state_optimizer only accepts SELLA)

param.ts.irc.title: Run IRC
param.ts.irc.does: Follows each optimized TS downhill in both directions, giving the two minima it connects (irc*.xyz).
how: g-xTB/ASE engines: Sella's IRC from the TS, fmax 0.1 eV/Å, up to 1000 steps per direction; g-xTB runs both branches at once in two threads.
If Sella's inner loop fails on the first steps, it is retried once from the TS with keep_going.
Frames are aligned to remove rigid drift. Engines without their own IRC use geomeTRIC (irc.compute_irc_chain_with_geometric).

swap.where: used automatically for engines without compute_irc_chain (mepd/irc.py)

caveats: A failed IRC leaves the TS written, with irc_failed.txt saying why.

param.ts.minimize_ends.title: Minimize endpoints
param.ts.minimize_ends.does: Optimizes start and end at the job's level before the path is built, so the path connects real minima.
how: auto: minimize unless both structures are already optimized, ready, and at this job's level fingerprint (JobContext.at_job_level).
Uses the engine's geometry optimization (g-xTB: `gxtb --opt --cycles 500`), batched when the engine can (cli_common._minimize_endpoints).
A reported non-convergence stops the run; other failures keep the input geometry with a warning.
param.ts.minimize_ends.default: auto: a structure from another profile or a force-field embedding is re-minimized so both ends and the path share one surface.

param.ts.atom_mapping.title: Check atom mapping
param.ts.atom_mapping.does: Makes sure atom i in the start is atom i in the end; if another numbering fits better, the end's atoms are renumbered before the search.
how: SLAPMapper (Koda 2025) maps start to end (atom_mapping.check_atom_mapping).
Candidates: SLAPMapper's mappings plus relabelings of symmetric atoms (up to 200), plus Explore mechanisms if set (cli_common._candidate_atom_maps).
They are compared by the Mapping metric (atom_mapping_selection.select_best_candidate) and the best end numbering is used.
Off: SLAPMapper still checks and only reports.
param.ts.atom_mapping.default: On in the web form (the CLI default is off): a wrong numbering forces unphysical atom swaps onto the path.
caveats: Skipped for QM/MM systems and when atom counts differ; needs the slapmapper package.

param.ts.endpoints.title: Endpoint source
param.ts.endpoints.does: Chooses whether mepd gets the stored geometries or the SMILES the structures were entered as.
how: xyz: each structure's geometry (the chosen conformer, else the lowest one) is copied into the job's inputs folder.
smiles: both SMILES are passed; mepd maps the pair with SLAPMapper and embeds a consistently numbered 3D pair (atom_mapping.map_smiles_pair), then minimizes it.
auto: SMILES only when both were entered as SMILES and neither has been minimized yet; otherwise xyz.
param.ts.endpoints.default: auto: once a structure is minimized, that geometry is the structure.

param.ts.pair_from.title: Build endpoint
param.ts.pair_from.does: Replaces one endpoint with a geometry built in the other's frame, so only the atoms that react move along the path.
how: The target's bonds are embedded on the source's atom positions (each atom stays, new bonds pulled to length; network_expansion.embed_product).
The built partner is minimized with the engine; it is dropped if its bonds or stereochemistry changed (network_expansion.build_partners).
With Check atom mapping on, one partner per candidate mechanism is built and minimized, and the pair with the best path wins (built_pair_mapping.build_and_rank).

swap.option: Product built from reactant / reactant built from product

caveats: The run fails if the built partner changes bonds on minimization.

param.ts.rebuild_splits_from.title: Rebuild at splits
param.ts.rebuild_splits_from.does: Experimental. At every recursive split, each new leg's product is rebuilt in its start's frame (or the start in its product's frame), so legs meet at different conformers of an intermediate.
how: After MSMEP makes the split's legs, each leg's other endpoint is built like 'Build endpoint' and minimized (MSMEP._rebuild_leg_endpoint).
The rebuilt endpoint is kept only if bonds and stereochemistry survive; otherwise the leg keeps the found endpoint.
param.ts.rebuild_splits_from.default: Off: legs end where the search found them.

param.ts.atom_mapping_metric.title: Mapping metric
param.ts.atom_mapping_metric.does: Sets how candidate atom mappings (and in channels, conformer pairs) are compared.
how: Snap + GI + xtb: candidates ranked by endpoint RMSD of snap's pick (reactant's symmetric groups permuted one at a time); for those kept, snap's few picks are geodesically interpolated and scored by GFN2-xTB energy along the path; the lowest peak wins.
Then the top 'Rank mappings' mechanisms are relaxed with changing bonds held (xtb --gfn 2) and compared by relaxed barrier.
Endpoint RMSD: aligned RMSD of the two ends. GI path: geodesic interpolation length. Filtered GI path: RMSD first, GI only near the lowest.
param.ts.atom_mapping_metric.default: snap-gi-xtb. Without xtb it falls back to the shortest interpolation, without interpolation to the lowest RMSD.

swap.option: Endpoint RMSD, GI path, Filtered GI path

caveats: xtb scoring uses GFN2-xTB from the xtb binary, not your profile's engine.

param.ts.explore_mechanisms.title: Explore mechanisms
param.ts.explore_mechanisms.does: Adds mechanisms beyond SLAPMapper's minimal bond-edit ones, e.g. a proton relayed through a catalyst or solvent, as candidates scored like the others.
how: Starting from SLAPMapper's mappings, swap the images of two same-element atoms or two groups, keeping swaps that add at most 2 bond edits; 5 rounds (atom_mapping.explore_mechanisms).
Up to N new routes, fewest edits first; ties: fewest H–C bond changes.
Each is scored by snap + GI + xtb; one that uses and regenerates a molecule is labelled [catalytic: ...].
caveats: A mechanism with more bond changes only wins if its relaxed barrier beats SLAPMapper's by more than the margin.

param.ts.relax_mechanisms.title: Rank mappings by relaxed path energy (top N)
param.ts.relax_mechanisms.does: Compares the best mappings by a relaxed barrier instead of the raw interpolation peak, which is mostly atoms colliding mid-path.
how: Takes the N best mechanisms by raw xtb peak, plus SLAPMapper's minimal one always (atom_mapping_selection._relaxed_choice).
Every 2nd interior frame and the peak are optimized with GFN2-xTB (xtb --gfn 2), with the distances of the bonds that change held fixed (_relaxed_barrier).
The lowest relaxed barrier wins, subject to the margin for extra bond changes.

param.ts.relax_margin.title: Margin for extra bond changes (kcal/mol)
param.ts.relax_margin.does: A mapping with more bond changes than SLAPMapper's minimal one must have a relaxed barrier lower by more than this, or SLAPMapper's mapping is kept.
how: Applied in atom_mapping_selection._relaxed_choice after the relaxed barriers are computed; the log lists every compared mechanism and the deciding rule.
param.ts.relax_margin.default: 5 kcal/mol (atom_mapping_inputs.relax_margin): a bias toward the minimal-edit mechanism.

param.ts.validate_minima_with_hessian.title: Validate minima with Hessian
param.ts.validate_minima_with_hessian.does: Every intermediate a recursive split proposes must be a true minimum; a saddle point is pushed off and re-optimized, or rejected as a split point.
how: Hessian of each optimized split candidate (g-xTB: `gxtb --hess --acc 0.001`, frequencies from its g98.out).
Accepted if the lowest frequency ≥ the cutoff (default −20 cm⁻¹).
Otherwise displaced ±0.3 bohr along the lowest mode, re-optimized and re-checked; the first that passes is used, else rejected (elementarystep._hessian_rescue_failed_candidate).
param.ts.validate_minima_with_hessian.default: On: a correctness check, so splits never happen at saddle points.

param.ts.hessian_minimum_frequency_cutof.title: Lowest allowed frequency (cm⁻¹)
param.ts.hessian_minimum_frequency_cutof.does: The threshold for calling a structure a minimum: its lowest frequency must be at or above this value (imaginary frequencies are negative).
how: Compared with min(frequencies) from the Hessian check (elementarystep._validate_hessian_minimum).
param.ts.hessian_minimum_frequency_cutof.default: −20 cm⁻¹: tolerates small numerical imaginary modes from soft torsions.

param.ts.network_completion.title: Network completion
param.ts.network_completion.does: After the search, runs extra path searches between intermediates the split tree found and the start/end, and builds one network from all of them.
how: Loads every structure in the split tree (NetworkBuilder).
linear: each intermediate paired with the original start and end; all-to-all: every pair. Pairs already joined by an edge are skipped.
Up to Max follow-ups pairs (default 25) run as recursive searches (cli_common._run_msmep_pairs); network.json is rebuilt from all trees.

param.ts.same_pair_split_limit.title: Same-pair split limit
param.ts.same_pair_split_limit.does: Stops splitting a branch that repeats the same start/end pair this many times in a row without finding new chemistry.
how: MSMEP counts consecutive splits of a branch that reproduce the same endpoint pair (MSMEP._consecutive_same_pair_split_count); a split that finds a new molecule or conformer is never cut off.
param.ts.same_pair_split_limit.default: 5. Raise it for floppy systems that need more attempts.

op.channels.title: Reaction channels
op.channels.does: Samples conformers of both ends and every atom mapping, searches each distinct mechanism, and sorts the TSs into direct, multi-step and off-target channels. Finds the lowest channel rather than the nearest one.
how: Minimizes SMILES endpoints, checks the endpoint atom mapping (SLAPMapper), then samples conformers (RDKit ETKDG + MMFF94, or CREST) and minimizes each with the engine; dedups by snap-RMSD and merges mirror images.
Pairs every reactant conformer with every product conformer; maps each pair per mechanism and keeps the best-scoring pairs per mechanism (_expand_pairs_by_mechanism).
Runs a recursive path search (MSMEP) per kept pair, in parallel processes.
TS optimization + IRC for every leaf, then classifies by walking the graph the IRCs span; equal TSs (energy + snap-RMSD) are merged (_discover_channels).
op.channels.default: RDKit conformers, 3 searches per mechanism, snap-gi-xtb mapping, 4 workers.

swap.option: Build one side from the other

swap.where: not exposed: --method only accepts 'conformers'; would plug in at mepd/sampling.py:generate_seed_pairs

caveats: Costly: number of path searches ≈ mechanisms × searches per mechanism.
Off-target channels end at products other than the requested one.
op.channels.cli: mepd channels --start a.xyz --end b.xyz --backend rdkit --pairs-per-mechanism 3 --workers 4 -i profile.toml

param.channels.backend.title: Conformer backend
param.channels.backend.does: Chooses the program that samples each endpoint's conformers before they are minimized at your level of theory.
how: rdkit: bonds perceived from the geometry (RDKit, else Open Babel), ETKDG embeddings with and without torsion preferences pooled, each relaxed with MMFF94 (conformers._generate_conformers_rdkit).
Embeddings: 50 / 200 / 300 for ≤7 / 8–12 / >12 rotatable bonds unless set.
crest: `crest <xyz> --gfn2 --ewin 6 -T 1` (iterative metadynamics), NCI mode for complexes, 3600 s limit.
Both: dedup by snap-RMSD (0.1 bohr), then every conformer is minimized with the engine and deduplicated again.
param.channels.backend.default: rdkit: seconds and no external program; CREST takes minutes per molecule.
caveats: If bond orders can't be perceived (radicals, unusual charges), RDKit keeps only the input geometry.

param.channels.pairs_per_mechanism.title: Searches per mechanism
param.channels.pairs_per_mechanism.does: How many conformer pairs get a path search for each bond-change mechanism; the rest are not searched.
how: Every reactant × product pair is mapped once per mechanism (atom_mapping_selection.select_per_mechanism), scored by the metric's first stage (snap endpoint RMSD for snap-gi-xtb).
Per mechanism, the K lowest-scoring pairs are kept.
For snap-gi-xtb, each kept pair's numbering is then chosen among snap's picks by GI + GFN2-xTB.
param.channels.pairs_per_mechanism.default: 3: pairs within a mechanism mostly converge to the same TS.

param.channels.built_cap_per_mechanism.title: Built searches per mechanism
param.channels.built_cap_per_mechanism.does: With built endpoints, applies the Built path searches cap to each mechanism instead of to all built pairs together.
how: Built pairs are ranked by the xtb peak along their interpolation, above the lowest start among them; the lowest per mechanism (on) or overall (off) are searched (cli_channels._choose_built_pairs).

param.channels.direct_only.title: Only legs touching start or end
param.channels.direct_only.does: When a path search splits, runs only the legs with at least one end at the start or end species; legs between two other species are skipped.
how: Sets path_min_inputs.direct_only; MSMEP drops split pieces whose both ends are other species (any conformer or stereoisomer of start/end counts) (MSMEP._split_pieces_on_target).
stats.json reports pairs left uncharacterized.
caveats: Multi-step routes through two unknown intermediates are not completed.

param.channels.minimize_ends.title: Minimize endpoints
param.channels.minimize_ends.does: Minimizes SMILES endpoints before sampling, and every sampled conformer before pairing, at the profile's level.

param.channels.minimize_ends.default: On: RDKit/MMFF conformers are not minima of your engine.

param.channels.reuse_conformers.does: Takes an endpoint's conformers from an earlier finished Reaction channels run on the same molecule instead of sampling and minimizing them again.

param.channels.pair_from.does: Pairs every reactant conformer with every product conformer, or samples one side and builds each conformer's partner in its frame, so only what reacts moves.
how: both: sampled × sampled pairs.

start / end / start+end: for each sampled conformer, a partner is built per candidate mechanism (atoms stay, new bonds pulled to length) and minimized; partners whose bonds or stereochemistry change are dropped.
All built pairs are ranked by the xtb peak along their interpolation; the lowest Built path searches (default 3) are searched. If none can be built, falls back to both.

Writes pair_mechanisms.json: pair, mechanism, score.

param.channels.atom_mapping_rmsd_window.does: Filtered GI path only: how many conformer pairs get a geodesic-interpolation score, by distance from each mechanism's lowest endpoint RMSD.
how: Every pair is first scored by endpoint RMSD.
Pairs within this many standard deviations of the mechanism's lowest RMSD get GI paths, for at most 20 lowest-RMSD symmetry variants each (cli_channels._gi_near_lowest_rmsd).

param.channels.crest_method.title: CREST method
param.channels.crest_method.does: The level CREST runs its metadynamics at.
how: Passed as CREST's level flag: `crest <xyz> --gfn2|--gfnff|--gfn2//gfnff --ewin 6 -T 1` (conformers._build_crest_argv). The result is then minimized at your profile's level.

param.channels.rmsd_cutoff.title: Dedup RMSD (bohr)
param.channels.rmsd_cutoff.does: Two conformers of one endpoint closer than this count as the same and one is dropped.
how: qcinf snap_rmsd: permutation-aware (symmetric atoms relabelled) and Kabsch-aligned (conformers._subselect_conformers); applied after sampling and again after minimization.

param.channels.n_conformers.title: Max conformers
param.channels.n_conformers.does: Caps each endpoint's pool after dedup.
how: If more remain, picks by farthest-point selection (each new pick farthest from those kept), not truncation (conformers._diverse_subset).
param.channels.n_conformers.default: 0 in the web form (no cap); the CLI default is 50.

op.channels-more.title: Sample more paths
op.channels-more.does: Extends a finished Reaction channels run with more conformer pairs per mechanism (or more built pairs), reusing its conformers and every path already searched.
how: Reruns the source job's exact command in its own output folder with a higher --pairs-per-mechanism and its saved start_pool/end_pool (operations._build_channels_more).
Pair labels come from pair_mechanisms.json, so finished pairs are found by folder name and skipped.
Built-endpoint runs: reruns on the saved built_pairs list with a higher --atom-mapping-candidates, or exactly the entries named.
TS/IRC and classification then run over all pairs.
op.channels-more.default: 6 per mechanism; for built runs 3 more searches.
caveats: Older runs without saved pools or pair table cannot be extended.

param.channels-more.pairs_per_mechanism.title: Searches per mechanism
param.channels-more.pairs_per_mechanism.does: The new per-mechanism cap; must exceed the old one (or 0 = all pairs).
how: Replaces --pairs-per-mechanism in the source run's command; already searched pairs keep their labels and are skipped.

param.channels-more.path_searches.title: Built path searches
param.channels-more.path_searches.does: Runs with built endpoints: the new total cap on path searches, so the next built pairs down the ranked list are searched.
how: Passes --built-pairs <out>/built_pairs and --atom-mapping-candidates <cap>; --max-pairs is dropped (operations._channels_more_built).

param.channels-more.rmsd_window.title: RMSD window (σ)
param.channels-more.rmsd_window.does: Filtered GI path only: widen the window so more conformer pairs get GI-scored.
how: Replaces --atom-mapping-rmsd-window in the rerun.

op.tsopt.title: Optimize TS from guess
op.tsopt.does: Treats the structure as a TS guess: optimizes it to a first-order saddle point and, by default, follows its IRC to the two minima it connects.
how: The structure (or design) is written as guess.xyz and `mepd ts --guess` runs with the job's profile.
engine.compute_transition_state: for g-xTB and ASE engines, Sella (order 1, fmax 0.01 eV/Å, up to 500 steps); for QCCompute engines, geomeTRIC's transition_state.
With IRC: Sella IRC both ways (fmax 0.1 eV/Å, 1000 steps), or geomeTRIC IRC for engines without one.
op.tsopt.default: IRC on (the CLI default is off).
caveats: The result is not Hessian-checked here; check the imaginary-mode count before trusting it.

param.tsopt.irc.does: Follows each optimized TS downhill in both directions, giving the two minima it connects (irc*.xyz).

If Sella's inner loop fails on the first steps, it is retried once from the TS with keep_going.
Frames are aligned to remove rigid drift. Engines without their own IRC use geomeTRIC (irc.compute_irc_chain_with_geometric).
param.tsopt.irc.default: On in the web form; the CLI default is off.

caveats: A failed IRC leaves the TS written, with irc_failed.txt saying why.

op.design-tsopt.title: Optimize the design as a TS
op.design-tsopt.does: Treats the Design tab's molecule as a TS guess: saddle optimization, then an IRC to the reactant and product it connects. If it does not converge, the design goes back to the submitted structure.
how: The design's molblock is converted to xyz (web.design.to_xyz) and written as inputs/guess.xyz.
engine.compute_transition_state: for g-xTB and ASE engines, Sella (order 1, fmax 0.01 eV/Å, up to 500 steps); for QCCompute engines, geomeTRIC's transition_state.
With IRC: Sella IRC both ways (fmax 0.1 eV/Å, 1000 steps), or geomeTRIC IRC for engines without one.

swap.where: the workspace level of theory (or the profile passed)

param.design-tsopt.irc.title: Run IRC
param.design-tsopt.irc.does: Follows each optimized TS downhill in both directions, giving the two minima it connects (irc*.xyz).
how: g-xTB/ASE engines: Sella's IRC from the TS, fmax 0.1 eV/Å, up to 1000 steps per direction; g-xTB runs both branches at once in two threads.
If Sella's inner loop fails on the first steps, it is retried once from the TS with keep_going.
Frames are aligned to remove rigid drift. Engines without their own IRC use geomeTRIC (irc.compute_irc_chain_with_geometric).
param.design-tsopt.irc.default: On in the web form; the CLI default is off.

swap.where: used automatically for engines without compute_irc_chain (mepd/irc.py)

caveats: A failed IRC leaves the TS written, with irc_failed.txt saying why.

op.optimize.title: Optimize geometry
op.optimize.does: Minimizes the selected structures at the chosen profile's level, replacing their geometry and energy in place.
how: Runs `mepd optimize` on snapshots of the structures with the job's profile; one job per charge/spin group.

engine.compute_geometry_optimization; g-xTB: `gxtb --opt --cycles 500` per structure, run in parallel, SCF retried with Fermi smearing if it oscillates; ASE engines: ASE LBFGSLineSearch, fmax 0.01 eV/Å.
Optional Hessian check with rescue (elementarystep.validate_minimum_with_rescue).
Geometry, energy and level replace the structure's in place; if bonds changed it is flagged 'reacted while being minimized' (Workspace.apply_optimization).
op.optimize.default: Hessian check follows the workspace 'Confirm minima with a Hessian' switch (on).
caveats: Transition states are refused (use Optimize TS from guess).
A converged saddle point is kept but flagged 'not a minimum'.

param.optimize.validate_minima_with_hess.title: Verify minima with Hessian
param.optimize.validate_minima_with_hess.does: After optimizing, requires no imaginary frequency below the cutoff; a structure stuck on a saddle is pushed off and re-optimized, else flagged 'not a minimum'.
how: Hessian at the optimized geometry; g-xTB: `gxtb --hess --acc 0.001`, frequencies from its g98.out.
Minimum if the lowest frequency ≥ −20 cm⁻¹ (cutoff).
Else displaced ±0.3 bohr along the lowest mode, re-optimized and re-checked; the first that passes replaces the geometry (validate_minimum_with_rescue).
caveats: For large or floppy structures (explicit solvent) the Hessian and rescue can take minutes.

param.optimize.hessian_minimum_frequency.title: Lowest allowed frequency (cm⁻¹)
param.optimize.hessian_minimum_frequency.does: The threshold for calling a structure a minimum: its lowest frequency must be at or above this value (imaginary frequencies are negative).
how: Compared with min(frequencies) from the Hessian check (elementarystep._validate_hessian_minimum).
param.optimize.hessian_minimum_frequency.default: −20 cm⁻¹: tolerates small numerical imaginary modes from soft torsions.

param.optimize.hessian_minima_rescue_dis.title: Rescue push (bohr)
param.optimize.hessian_minima_rescue_dis.does: How far a structure that failed the Hessian check is displaced along its lowest mode, both ways, before re-optimizing.
how: displace_by_dr along the lowest-frequency normal mode by +d and −d; each is re-optimized and re-checked; no larger pushes are retried (elementarystep._hessian_rescue_failed_candidate).
param.optimize.hessian_minima_rescue_dis.default: 0.3 bohr. Larger pushes on g-xTB mostly fell back to the same soft saddle.

op.design-optimize.title: Minimize the design
op.design-optimize.does: Minimizes the Design tab's molecule at the chosen profile's level; its geometry and energy are replaced in place.
how: The design's molblock is converted to xyz (web.design.to_xyz) and written as inputs/design.xyz.

engine.compute_geometry_optimization; g-xTB: `gxtb --opt --cycles 500` per structure, run in parallel, SCF retried with Fermi smearing if it oscillates; ASE engines: ASE LBFGSLineSearch, fmax 0.01 eV/Å.
Optional Hessian check with rescue (elementarystep.validate_minimum_with_rescue).
op.design-optimize.default: Hessian check follows the workspace 'Confirm minima with a Hessian' switch.
caveats: A reaction design is not minimized here: its ends are minimized when the path search starts.

param.design-optimize.validate_minima_wi.title: Verify minima with Hessian
param.design-optimize.validate_minima_wi.does: After optimizing, requires no imaginary frequency below the cutoff; a structure stuck on a saddle is pushed off and re-optimized, else flagged 'not a minimum'.
how: Hessian at the optimized geometry; g-xTB: `gxtb --hess --acc 0.001`, frequencies from its g98.out.
Minimum if the lowest frequency ≥ −20 cm⁻¹ (cutoff).
Else displaced ±0.3 bohr along the lowest mode, re-optimized and re-checked; the first that passes replaces the geometry (validate_minimum_with_rescue).
caveats: For large or floppy structures (explicit solvent) the Hessian and rescue can take minutes.

op.network-splits.title: Paths between isomers
op.network-splits.does: Searches a path between every pair of the selected isomers and joins the steps found, with any intermediates, into one network.
how: Snapshots each structure; all must share atoms, charge and spin (operations._build_network_splits).
Forms every pair (all-to-all), skipping pairs with identical connectivity; at most Max pairs (default 100).
Runs a recursive path search (MSMEP) for each pair (cli_common._run_msmep_pairs).
Builds network.json from all completed split trees (NetworkBuilder.create_rxn_network_from_paths).
op.network-splits.default: All-to-all pairing, sequential branches, Hessian validation on.
caveats: No TS optimization or IRC here: edges come from path searches.
op.network-splits.cli: mepd network-splits a.xyz b.xyz c.xyz --max-pairs 100 -i profile.toml

param.network-splits.parallel.title: Parallel branches
param.network-splits.parallel.does: Runs each pair's split branches concurrently.
how: MSMEP.run_parallel_recursive_minimize with up to min(4, CPUs) workers (threads; processes for local QCCompute).

param.network-splits.validate_minima_wit.title: Validate minima with Hessian
param.network-splits.validate_minima_wit.does: Every intermediate a recursive split proposes must be a true minimum; a saddle point is pushed off and re-optimized, or rejected as a split point.
how: Hessian of each optimized split candidate (g-xTB: `gxtb --hess --acc 0.001`, frequencies from its g98.out).
Accepted if the lowest frequency ≥ the cutoff (default −20 cm⁻¹).
Otherwise displaced ±0.3 bohr along the lowest mode, re-optimized and re-checked; the first that passes is used, else rejected (elementarystep._hessian_rescue_failed_candidate).
param.network-splits.validate_minima_wit.default: On: a correctness check, so splits never happen at saddle points.

op.vri.title: Valley-ridge inflection
op.vri.does: Scans the IRC from this edge's TS for a valley-ridge transition, where the path can split after the TS into two products (P1, P2), and tests whether it really bifurcates.
how: Takes the lowest IRC-verified TS known for the edge (operations.edge_route_ts); checks it has an imaginary mode.
Tight IRC (Sella dx 0.05, fmax 0.01 eV/Å), Hessians along it; lowest frequency orthogonal to the path (Miller–Handy–Adams projection); sign change bisected → VRT (vri.scan_irc_for_vrt).
Pushes along the ridge mode past the VRT and optimizes to find P2; searches TS2 between P1 and P2.
Basin test: sideways pushes off the IRC drained by optimization; split into P1 and P2 = bifurcation. Repeats from symmetrized TS1 candidates.
op.vri.default: Both branches, Hessian every 2nd IRC point, TS2 search, symmetrized TS1, exact VRI on, 4 parallel Hessians.

swap.where: Trajectories from TS1 (advanced) or Check the bifurcation

caveats: When the VRI lies off the IRC, projected frequencies may never turn imaginary; trajectories can still split.

param.vri.branches.title: IRC branches
param.vri.branches.does: Which side(s) of TS1 are scanned for a valley-ridge transition.
how: The IRC is split at TS1 (vri.split_irc_branches); only the chosen branches get Hessians, product searches and checks.

param.vri.stride.title: Hessian every Nth IRC point
param.vri.stride.does: Sets how densely the IRC is scanned; the VRT is bracketed between scanned points and then bisected.
how: Hessian at every Nth IRC point; then n_bisect (default 4) bisection steps between the bracketing points (vri.scan_irc_for_vrt).
param.vri.stride.default: 2 in the web form (halves the cost); the CLI default is 1.

param.vri.find_ts2.title: Find TS2
param.vri.find_ts2.does: Searches for the second saddle (TS2) between P1 and P2 and verifies it.
how: auto: TS-optimize the top of the geodesic P1→P2 path; if that fails verification, relax the path with the profile's path method first (discovery.cli._locate_ts2).
Verified: one imaginary mode, below TS1, IRC connects P1 and P2, and ridge-connected to TS1 (downhill, no intermediate) (vri.verify_ts2, vri_candidates.ridge_connected).

param.vri.ts2_method.title: TS2 search
param.vri.ts2_method.does: How the TS2 guess between P1 and P2 is made.
how: geodesic: highest image of the geodesic P1→P2 interpolation, TS-optimized (seconds). neb: that path relaxed with the profile's path minimizer first. auto: geodesic, then NEB if not verified (discovery.cli._search_ts2).

param.vri.symmetric_ts.title: Try symmetrized TS1
param.vri.symmetric_ts.does: Also starts from TS1 candidates made by symmetrizing TS1 under near-symmetries of its bond graph; finds ridge saddles such as bispericyclic TSs.
how: Permutations of TS1's partial-bond graph (networkx GraphMatcher, up to 200) whose permuted geometry aligns onto TS1 within 0.05–1.0 Å count as near-symmetries.
Symmetrized geometries are re-optimized; distinct first-order saddles each get the full search in symmetric_<k>/ (vri_candidates.symmetric_ts_candidates).

param.vri.exact_vri.title: Converge the exact VRI
param.vri.exact_vri.does: From the VRT, converges to the exact valley-ridge inflection point (H v = 0, v perpendicular to the gradient) on every branch with a second product.
how: Gauss–Newton with the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse, after Schmidt & Quapp (vri_checks.refine_vri); writes vri_<branch>.xyz.
param.vri.exact_vri.default: On; a few seconds per branch.

param.vri.trajectories.title: Trajectories from TS1
param.vri.trajectories.does: Quasiclassical trajectories from TS1 into each confirmed bifurcation; counts P1 vs P2 for a product ratio.
how: Initial conditions: each real mode gets a Boltzmann-sampled quantum level (mostly zero-point) with random phase; the reaction mode gets Boltzmann kinetic energy toward the branch (Progdyn/Milo-style).
Velocity Verlet with engine gradients for the trajectory length (default 400 fs).
Each final frame is optimized and classified as P1, P2 or other (discovery.qct).
caveats: 100 trajectories resolve shares above a few percent.
param.vri.trajectories.default: 0 (none) in VRI search; run them only on confirmed bifurcations.

param.vri.hessian.title: Hessian source
param.vri.hessian.does: Chooses how the Hessians along the IRC (and at TS1, the VRI) are computed.
how: engine (= auto): the engine's own compute_hessian; for g-xTB one `gxtb --hess --acc 0.001` call with the rigid-body part restored from the gradient, ~2–4× cheaper.
gradients: central differences of engine gradients, step 0.005 bohr, 6N calls, shared concurrency limit (vri.GradientHessianEngine).
Only the VRI analysis uses the wrapper; IRC, path minimizers and TS optimizations use the plain engine.
caveats: g-xTB's --hess matrix can differ from its own gradients by ~0.02 Eh/bohr²; at non-stationary IRC points that can flip soft projected frequencies. Use gradients to confirm a borderline VRT.

param.vri.irc_step.title: IRC step (Å·amu½)
param.vri.irc_step.does: Step size of the tighter IRC the scan runs on; smaller resolves the VRT better.
how: Passed as Sella's dx for g-xTB/ASE engines (discovery.cli._run_vri_irc); other engines use their own IRC defaults, or geomeTRIC on failure.
param.vri.irc_step.default: 0.05, with stopping force 0.01 eV/Å (mepd's usual IRC uses Sella defaults and fmax 0.1).

param.vri.vrt_threshold.title: Imaginary threshold (cm⁻¹)
param.vri.vrt_threshold.does: A projected frequency must fall below minus this value to count as imaginary along the IRC.
how: Used with Consecutive imaginary points (default 2) to reject noise when locating the VRT (vri.scan_irc_for_vrt).

param.vri.max_vrt_depth.title: Max VRT depth below TS1 (kcal/mol)
param.vri.max_vrt_depth.does: Imaginary dips more than this far below TS1 are reported as late softening, not a VRT.
how: Applied in vri.scan_irc_for_vrt; deep in a product valley a soft torsion is not a bifurcation of TS1.

param.vri.push_amplitude.title: Ridge push (bohr)
param.vri.push_amplitude.does: How far points past the VRT are displaced along the ridge mode, both ways, before optimizing to find P2.
how: Largest single-atom move; pushes from 3 points (the VRT and after), each optimized with the engine (vri.find_bifurcation_products).

op.vri-check.title: Check the bifurcation
op.vri-check.does: For a finished VRI search: converges the exact VRI, tests that sideways pushes off the IRC drain into both P1 and P2, and counts trajectories into each.
how: For every branch with a VRT or second product (vri_checks.check_branch):
Exact VRI: Gauss–Newton with pseudoinverse to H v = 0, v ⊥ gradient (Schmidt & Quapp).
Basin test: at 5 IRC points, displacements 0.05/0.1/0.2/0.3 bohr both ways along the softest perpendicular mode, then optimized; outcomes P1, P2, R or other.
Quasiclassical trajectories from TS1 (default 150, 400 fs); the verdict is updated (vri.verdict_after_checks).
op.vri-check.default: All three checks on, 150 trajectories, 4 parallel engine calls.
caveats: If the search found no P2, the first other product the basin test reaches becomes P2.

param.vri-check.trajectories.title: Trajectories from TS1
param.vri-check.trajectories.does: Quasiclassical trajectories from TS1 into each confirmed bifurcation; counts P1 vs P2 for a product ratio.
how: Initial conditions: each real mode gets a Boltzmann-sampled quantum level (mostly zero-point) with random phase; the reaction mode gets Boltzmann kinetic energy toward the branch (Progdyn/Milo-style).
Velocity Verlet with engine gradients for the trajectory length (default 400 fs).
Each final frame is optimized and classified as P1, P2 or other (discovery.qct).
caveats: 100 trajectories resolve shares above a few percent.

param.vri-check.refine.title: Converge the exact VRI
param.vri-check.refine.does: From the VRT, converges to the exact valley-ridge inflection point (H v = 0, v perpendicular to the gradient) on every branch with a second product.
how: Gauss–Newton with the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse, after Schmidt & Quapp (vri_checks.refine_vri); writes vri_<branch>.xyz.
param.vri-check.refine.default: On; a few seconds per branch.

param.vri-check.basin.title: Basin test
param.vri-check.basin.does: Optimizes from sideways pushes off the IRC past TS1; a real bifurcation drains into both P1 and P2. This test decides the verdict.
how: At IRC points past TS1, displace along the softest perpendicular mode (and the second where also imaginary) by 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 bohr, both ways.
Optimize each with the engine; classify the end as P1, P2, R (reactant side), P3… or failed (vri_checks.basin_test).
caveats: Symmetry-equivalent products can appear as P3.

op.vri-surface.title: Map the 2D surface
op.vri-surface.does: Reconstructs the energy surface around each bifurcation, with TS1, VRI, TS2, P1 and P2 on one map, from a relaxed 2D scan.
how: Axes: x = displacement along TS1's imaginary mode (Å); y = mean length of P2-only bonds minus P1-only bonds (Å).

At each grid node, an engine optimization (scipy L-BFGS-B, steps boxed to 0.4 Å) with harmonic restraints (3000 kcal/mol/Å²) on x, y and the other reactive bonds, from the nearest computed structure (vri_surface.relaxed_grid).
IRCs and stationary points are overlaid as an independent check; writes surface_<branch>.json.
caveats: Partially relaxed scan: passes and basins are approximate; check that the overlaid stationary points sit on them.
Only branches with a P2 are mapped.

param.vri-surface.grid.title: Grid nodes per axis
param.vri-surface.grid.does: Resolution of the map; each node is one restrained optimization, so cost grows with its square.
how: grid × grid restrained optimizations (vri_surface.relaxed_grid), run Parallel gradient calls at a time.

level.profile.title: Level of theory
level.profile.does: Sets the profile (a RunInputs TOML) every structure in the workspace is minimized at and new jobs run with, so energies are comparable.
how: PUT /api/level stores the profile; new structures, re-optimizations and design jobs use it by default (app.queue_optimization).
Each profile gets a level fingerprint: engine, method/model and implicit solvent only; threads, optimizer and path settings are left out (workspace.effective_level).
Structures whose fingerprint differs are counted as off-level; 're-optimize' minimizes them at this level.
Each node's representative conformer is re-picked; energies from different levels are never compared.
level.profile.default: The 'default' profile, seeded by `mepd init`: g-xTB (gxtb, fetched on first use) with NEB.

swap.option: Other engines: xTB, MLIPs (AIMNet2, ORB, UMA), FAIR-Chem, ASE calculators, Psi4, TeraChem, QCCompute/ChemCloud
A different profile for one job
swap.where: Compute profile in a job's form

caveats: Changing it doesn't re-optimize anything by itself.

level.validate_minima.title: Confirm minima with a Hessian
level.validate_minima.does: After a structure is minimized at the workspace level, checks it has no imaginary frequency beyond 20i cm⁻¹; a structure on a saddle is pushed off and re-minimized, else flagged 'not a minimum'.
how: Stored in workspace.json; passed as validate_minima_with_hessian to automatic Optimize jobs and design minimization.
Hessian at the optimized geometry (g-xTB: `gxtb --hess --acc 0.001`, frequencies from g98.out); minimum if lowest ≥ −20 cm⁻¹.
Else ±0.3 bohr along the lowest mode, re-optimized, re-checked (validate_minimum_with_rescue).
A failed node keeps its geometry, status 'not_minimum', and never represents the node.
level.validate_minima.default: On: roughly one Hessian per structure, and it catches structures stuck on saddles.
caveats: Path searches have their own 'Validate minima with Hessian' for split intermediates.

op.conformers.title: Conformers
op.conformers.does: Samples other 3D shapes of the selected molecule, keeps the distinct ones, and, by default, minimizes each at the profile's level. They join the node as conformers. The lowest-energy one then stands for the molecule.
how: Sample with RDKit (ETKDGv3 + MMFF94) or CREST (crest subprocess). mepd/conformers.py:generate_conformers

The input geometry is always kept first. Candidates closer than the RMSD cutoff (qcinf snap_rmsd: symmetry-aware, Kabsch-aligned, bohr) to one already kept are dropped. Candidates that are not isomorphic to the input are discarded.
If more than 'Keep at most' remain, a farthest-point (max-min RMSD) subset is kept. The list is not just cut off by energy (_diverse_subset).
With 'Minimize' on, `mepd optimize` runs on each one at the profile's level. Optionally each gets a Hessian check.
The web app adds each one to the node (app.py:attach conformers). Energies count only if they were minimized. A conformer that minimized into a different molecule is skipped.
op.conformers.default: RDKit sampler, keep 20, minimize on, Hessian check off, RMSD cutoff 0.1 bohr. RDKit takes seconds and needs nothing extra installed.

swap.where: Sampler: CREST in this form (needs `crest` on PATH)
not exposed: add a backend branch in mepd/conformers.py:generate_conformers

caveats: Sampler energies (MMFF, CREST) are not mepd energies. Without minimizing, the conformers have no energy and cannot represent the node.
Transition states are refused: conformers are sampled for minima only.

param.conformers.backend.title: Sampler
param.conformers.backend.does: Chooses the program that generates conformer candidates.
how: RDKit: ETKDGv3 embeddings, with and without experimental torsion preferences (pooled, so e.g. s-cis dienes appear). The input counts as conformer 0.
The embedding budget depends on rotatable bonds: 50 for 7 or fewer, 200 for 8–12, 300 above (_auto_n_embed). Each embedding is then relaxed with MMFF94 (maxIters 2000).
For several molecules, each fragment is aligned back to where it sits in the input (Kabsch).

CREST: `crest input.xyz <level> --ewin <window> -T 1`, plus --chrg/--uhf. --nci is added automatically for more than one molecule. Atoms must come back in the input order; frames that don't are dropped. Timeout 3600 s.
param.conformers.backend.default: RDKit: seconds, nothing to install. CREST takes minutes and runs single-threaded.

swap.where: Sampler: CREST (only if `crest` is on PATH)

caveats: The RDKit embedding seed is fixed (random_seed 0), so rerunning with the same settings gives the same pool.

param.conformers.minimize.title: Minimize at the profile's level
param.conformers.minimize.does: Re-optimizes every kept conformer with the profile's engine, so their energies can be compared and the lowest can represent the molecule.
how: Calls mepd.cli.optimize on conformers.xyz, writing to optimized/.
With 'Hessian-check each', the frequency cutoff is -20 cm⁻¹ and the rescue push is 0.3 bohr (fixed values in cli_conformers.py).
The web app keeps a minimized conformer's energy only if it still has the node's SMILES.
param.conformers.minimize.default: On. Without it there are no mepd energies, so the conformers are geometry only.

param.conformers.crest_method.title: CREST level
param.conformers.crest_method.does: Sets CREST's own Hamiltonian for the metadynamics. This is not mepd's level of theory.
how: Passed straight to crest as its level flag: --gfn2, --gfnff (force field, much faster) or --gfn2//gfnff (GFN-FF sampling, GFN2 reranking).
caveats: Conformers are re-minimized at the profile's level afterwards if 'Minimize' is on, so this only changes which shapes are found.

param.conformers.rmsd_cutoff.title: Distinct beyond RMSD (bohr)
param.conformers.rmsd_cutoff.does: Two candidates count as the same conformer if their RMSD is below this.
how: Uses qcinf snap_rmsd (permutation/symmetry-aware, Kabsch-aligned, bohr). The dedup runs to completion before any cap is applied (_subselect_conformers).

op.hessian-sample.title: Hessian sampling
op.hessian-sample.does: Finds the minima one vibration away from the structure (conformers, nearby isomers): it displaces along every normal mode in both directions and re-optimizes.
how: Compute the seed's energy and its Hessian with the profile's engine (engine._compute_hessian_result or compute_hessian). Program Hessians come via qcop. ASE/MLIP engines use central differences of gradients.
prepare_modes drops translations and rotations, sorts modes by frequency (imaginary first), and normalizes them.
Displace ± along each mode until 'Max candidates' is reached (low frequencies first). Each displaced geometry is optimized with the engine (batch if supported; Cartesian coordinates; maxiter 500).
Classify each result: back to seed, found before, or new minimum. Deduplicate with is_identical (graph + RunInputs node_rms_thre/node_ene_thre).
Optionally Hessian-check each unique minimum. Saddles get a push along the unstable mode, are re-optimized, or are rejected.
op.hessian-sample.default: Fixed-Cartesian displacement 0.1 bohr per-atom RMS, 100 candidates, Hessian validation on (the web default; off in the CLI).
caveats: Minima are merged by graph identity plus loose thresholds (node_rms_thre 5 bohr, node_ene_thre 5 kcal/mol by default), so close conformers may count as one.
One Hessian plus up to 100 optimizations: cost grows quickly with size at a DFT level.

param.hessian-sample.amplitude_policy.title: Displacement policy
param.hessian-sample.amplitude_policy.does: Sets how far each normal mode is pushed before re-optimizing.
how: fixed-cartesian: every mode moves the same distance. That is the per-atom RMS dr (bohr), scaled by sqrt(N atoms) on the 3N vector (_effective_dr).
energy: each mode's amplitude is a = sqrt(2 E_target / k), with k = uᵀHu from the Hessian. Each push then costs about E_target in the harmonic approximation.
Under energy, modes with k < 1e-4 Eh/bohr² are skipped. Imaginary modes get the fixed 'Imaginary-mode amplitude' (0.3 bohr).
param.hessian-sample.amplitude_policy.default: fixed-cartesian, 0.1 bohr: simple and independent of the Hessian's quality. It can over-stretch stiff bonds or under-push soft torsions; 'energy' evens that out.

param.hessian-sample.validate_minima_wit.title: Validate minima with Hessian
param.hessian-sample.validate_minima_wit.does: Keeps only true minima. A structure that stopped on a saddle point is pushed off it and re-optimized, or is dropped as rejected.
how: A Hessian of each unique minimum at the profile's level. It passes if the lowest frequency is at or above the cutoff (elementarystep.validate_minimum_with_rescue).
On failure: push ± the rescue displacement along the lowest mode, re-optimize, and check again.
The survivors are deduplicated again, since a rescue can land on a minimum already found.
param.hessian-sample.validate_minima_wit.default: On, with a cutoff of -20 cm⁻¹ and a 0.3 bohr push.
caveats: One extra Hessian per minimum (two if rescued).

op.hessian-global.title: Hessian basin hopping
op.hessian-global.does: Repeats Hessian sampling from every accepted minimum, accepting new minima by the Metropolis test. It is a breadth-first global search over the minima reachable from the seed.
how: Round 1 Hessian-samples the seed (run_hessian_sample, fixed-Cartesian dr). Later rounds sample every minimum accepted in the round before.
Each candidate minimum is compared with the acceptance baseline. Differences within 'Energy tolerance' count as flat. Uphill moves are accepted with probability exp(-ΔE/RT).
Minima already accepted (is_identical, including the seed) are skipped. Only Hessian-validated minima are accepted when validation is on.
Stops when no new minimum is accepted (queue exhausted) or after 'Max rounds'.
op.hessian-global.default: Up to 100 rounds, 298.15 K, 'connected' baseline, dr 0.1 bohr, 100 candidates per source, validation on.

swap.where: Advanced › Full displacement scan + Scan values
not exposed here: only in Hessian sampling (run_hessian_global_optimization has no amplitude_policy)

caveats: The search is breadth-first: every accepted minimum is a new source, so cost can grow fast. Max rounds is the only hard limit.
Without a random seed the accept/reject draws are not reproducible. With one, each draw is a hash of (seed, index).
op.hessian-global.cli: mepd discovery hessian-global seed.xyz -i level.toml --max-rounds 100 --temperature 298.15 --acceptance-baseline connected

param.hessian-global.acceptance_baseline.title: Acceptance baseline
param.hessian-global.acceptance_baseline.does: Sets the energy each new minimum's Metropolis test is measured against.
how: connected: the minimum it was sampled from (standard basin hopping).
seed: always the original seed. Seeded from a high-energy structure, everything then looks downhill and is accepted.
running_best: the lowest energy found so far. This is greedier.
param.hessian-global.acceptance_baseline.default: connected. The baseline follows the search, so the test keeps discriminating.

param.hessian-global.temperature.title: Temperature (K)
param.hessian-global.temperature.does: Sets how readily uphill minima are accepted: P = exp(-ΔE/RT). It is a search knob, not a physical condition.
how: Used only in _boltzmann_acceptance_probability. R comes from qcconst (CODATA).
param.hessian-global.temperature.default: 298.15 K. At this temperature a 2 kcal/mol uphill step is accepted about 3% of the time.

op.graph-enumeration.title: Reaction network expansion
op.graph-enumeration.does: Proposes products of the selected species, optimizes them at the profile's level, and adds the new species and proposed reactions to Explore. With more rounds, the network grows from the species that the kinetics (or an energy window) say matter.
how: The seed is minimized first (and Hessian-checked), so every energy is relative to a minimum at this level.
The product generator proposes products in the seed's atom order. Bond rules: up to n breaks and m formations. Alternatives: CREST msreact or nanoreactor MD.
For bond rules, each product's 3D guess is a restrained relaxation of the seed geometry onto the new bonds (embed_product, mepd's own heuristic).
Each guess is optimized with the engine. Species identity is connectivity + stereo; the lowest conformer is kept. New species can be Hessian-validated.
steer=flux: each reaction gets a recursive path search (MSMEP), TS opt and IRC. Eyring first-order microkinetics from the seed then picks which species to expand next.
op.graph-enumeration.default: Bond rules, 1 round, 2 breaks / 2 forms, 50 proposals per species, 60 kcal/mol window, no path search.

swap.where: Method switch: CREST msreact (needs crest + xtb)
CLI: mepd discovery expand --generator package.module:function, or --products file.xyz
not exposed in the UI: mepd/discovery/generators.py:GENERATORS

caveats: Without 'Connect by path search' (or flux), edges are proposals with no barrier yet.
Flux barriers are electronic, not free energies, each from the species' lowest conformer.

param.graph-enumeration.generator.title: Product generator
param.graph-enumeration.generator.does: Chooses what proposes the products. Everything after that (optimization, identity, edges, path searches) is the same for every generator.
how: Bond rules (mepd): every combination of ≤ n breaks and ≤ m formations between atoms within 'Form bonds within' (4 Å). Products must pass coordination limits and have an RDKit DetermineBondOrders (xyz2mol) Lewis structure. Fewest changes first; at most 500,000 combinations.
CREST msreact: `crest --msreact -T 1 -msnbonds n` (plus -msnoiso / -msiso by mode). Biased GFN2-xTB optimizations; products are ranked lowest GFN2 energy first.
Nanoreactor (QM/MM systems only): hot piston MD of the QM region. Its state after each event is a product.
param.graph-enumeration.generator.default: Bond rules: built in, deterministic, nothing to install.

swap.where: Method switch on the Network card
CLI: --generator package.module:function (returns product Structures in the same atom order)

caveats: msreact fragments one molecule only: a cluster of several gets no products.
param.graph-enumeration.generator.cli: mepd discovery expand seed.xyz --generator crest-msreact --generator-option mode=all

param.graph-enumeration.steer.title: Grow the network by
param.graph-enumeration.steer.does: Decides which new species get expanded in the next round.
how: window: every new species within 'Expand species within' (kcal/mol) of the seed.

flux: each new reaction gets a recursive path search (MSMEP), TS optimization and IRC. Then k = (kBT/h)·exp(-ΔE‡/RT) both ways from one TS energy, so detailed balance holds; this is integrated from pure seed over the simulated time.
A species is expanded once the material that flowed into it reaches the threshold (Bensberg–Reiher concentration flux). Growth stops when nothing new does.
auto: flux when rounds > 1, else window.
param.graph-enumeration.steer.default: auto (so window for 1 round). Flux defaults: 298.15 K, 3600 s, threshold 0.01.
caveats: Flux runs a TS search for every proposed reaction each round, which makes it far slower than window.

param.graph-enumeration.connect.title: Connect by path search
param.graph-enumeration.connect.does: Runs a recursive path search for each proposed reaction that reached a new species. Edges then carry real paths, not just proposals.
how: Runs mepd's recursive MSMEP over the species pairs, as in `mepd network-splits` (cli_common._run_msmep_pairs), capped at 'Max path searches'. It builds network.json from the resulting trees.
param.graph-enumeration.connect.default: Off: proposals come back fast. Run 'Find TS' on the ones you care about.
caveats: With steer=flux the path searches run anyway (each round); this switch is then implied.

op.retrosynthesis.title: Retrosynthesis
op.retrosynthesis.does: Searches for routes from purchasable building blocks to the target. The best route's steps join Explore as proposed reactions (no barriers unless checked).
how: The chosen method proposes single steps for a molecule.
AND-OR best-first search in the manner of Retro*. A step costs -log(score); a molecule in stock costs 0; an unsolved molecule is estimated by its SA score (mepd/retro/search.py).
Molecules in the stock, or with ≤ 2 heavy atoms, count as available. The search stops at the budget (100 expansions or 120 s); the 5 cheapest solved routes are reported.
Optionally, each step is balanced and atom-mapped (SLAPMapper), then `mepd run --recursive --use-tsopt --irc --minimize-ends` at the profile's level.
The web adds route 1 to Explore (web/retro.py:adopt_best_route). The others are added from the result page.
op.retrosynthesis.default: Templates method, automatic stock, verify off.

swap.where: Method switch on the Network card
not exposed: add a Proposer to mepd/retro/proposers.py:PROPOSERS
CLI only: mepd retro plan --value zero

caveats: Route cost is model confidence, not chemistry. Barriers exist only for verified steps.
Everything runs locally; data and weights download on first use.

param.retrosynthesis.method.title: Method
param.retrosynthesis.method.does: Chooses the single-step model that proposes disconnections. The route search around it is the same, except for AiZynthFinder.
how: Templates: rdchiral applies USPTO templates. AiZynthFinder's ONNX policy (onnxruntime, CPU) ranks the top 50 (cumulative 0.995); its filter network drops outcomes below 0.05. Without onnxruntime, templates are ranked by USPTO frequency.
ReactionT5: sagawa/ReactionT5v2-retrosynthesis via transformers, beam 10. Metal and carbon-free ions become reagents. Optional forward-model round-trip check.
Local LLM: an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions call with a JSON prompt. RDKit keeps only valid answers whose reactants supply the target's heavy atoms.
AiZynthFinder: its own MCTS run as a separate program, in its own environment.
param.retrosynthesis.method.default: Templates: seconds on CPU, ~110 MB of data on first use.

swap.where: CLI: mepd retro plan --option model=<HF id>

param.retrosynthesis.stock.title: Building blocks
param.retrosynthesis.stock.does: Sets what a route may start from. A molecule in the stock ends a branch at zero cost.
how: PaRoutes: the n1 and n5 building-block sets together (downloaded, 0.8 MB).
ZINC: AiZynthFinder's in-stock InChIKeys (after `mepd retro setup --aizynthfinder`), matched without stereo.
Automatic passes no --stock: the CLI uses ZINC if it is set up, else PaRoutes n1+n5 (cli_retro._default_stock).
'Also these (file)' adds your SMILES/InChIKey list. Molecules with ≤ 'Small molecules' heavy atoms (2) also count as available.
caveats: Automatic plus a file sends '--stock auto --stock <file>'. stock.load does not know 'auto' and fails. Pick PaRoutes or ZINC explicitly when adding a file.
param.retrosynthesis.stock.cli: mepd retro plan '<SMILES>' --stock paroutes-n1 --stock paroutes-n5 --stock my_blocks.txt --max-heavy 2

param.retrosynthesis.verify.title: Check steps with path searches
param.retrosynthesis.verify.does: Gives route steps real barriers: path search, TS and IRC at the profile's level. Without it, steps are proposals only.
how: Each step is balanced with byproducts and co-reactants (chem.balance_step). An unbalanceable step is shown but not verified.
Runs `mepd run --reaction 'A.B>>P.X' --recursive --use-tsopt --irc --minimize-ends` per step. SLAPMapper maps the atoms.
A barrier counts as verified only when the IRC connects start to end.
param.retrosynthesis.verify.default: Off: routes come back in seconds. Verification takes minutes to hours per step.

param.retrosynthesis.roundtrip.title: Round-trip check
param.retrosynthesis.roundtrip.does: Lowers the rank of ReactionT5 proposals that its forward model cannot turn back into the target.
how: sagawa/ReactionT5v2-forward predicts the top 3 products of each proposal (with its reagents). If the target is not among them, the proposal keeps 0.2 of its score (_ReactionT5._roundtrip).
param.retrosynthesis.roundtrip.default: On. It is a soft check: the forward model also misses valid reactions written without reagents.

op.nanoreactor.title: Nanoreactor
op.nanoreactor.does: Puts copies of the selected molecules in a hot sphere whose wall periodically squeezes them. Each reaction seen is cut out with only the molecules it needs, refined at your level, and added to Explore as a reaction dot.
how: Pack the molecules at random orientations in a sphere (sized from the atom count), then relax with the wall (xtb --opt crude, or engine steps).
Piston MD: wide for 75% of each 1 ps period, then closed to 0.6× over 100 fs. Soft logfermi wall at 20 kcal/mol/Å. Step 0.5 fs, frames every 2 fs.
Bonds come from Cordero radii with hysteresis (form < 1.15×, break > 1.45×). States shorter than 20 fs are ignored; changes within 100 fs on shared molecules are one event.

Each event's subsystem is the molecules whose bonds change (shuttles included). Its ends are cut out with the same atom order and optimized at the profile's level; each molecule is optimized alone too.
op.nanoreactor.default: 4 copies of each, 2000 K, 5 ps, MD on your level of theory, 3 occurrences refined per reaction.

swap.option: A different MD calculator than the refinement level

caveats: Energies are compared only within one reaction's subsystem; different reactions have different atoms.
High temperature finds what can happen, not what is fast at room temperature: get barriers from the TS searches.

param.nanoreactor.md_method.title: MD level
param.nanoreactor.md_method.does: Chooses what computes forces for the discovery MD. Refinement always uses the profile's level.
how: Your level of theory: run_engine_md. Langevin (BAOAB, friction 0.01/fs) with gradients from the profile's engine (MLIP, ASE, g-xTB...) and the same logfermi wall.
GFN2/GFN1/g-xTB: xtb's own --md per piston segment (nvt, hmass=1, no SHAKE). Electronic temperature 3000 K so bonds break cleanly; one thread.
Automatic: GFN2 if xtb is installed, else g-xTB if found, else your level (nanoreactor.pick_md_method).
Molecule charges for labeling always come from an xtb single point when xtb or g-xTB is present.
param.nanoreactor.md_method.default: Your level of theory: the MD sees the same chemistry as the rest of the workspace. The CLI's own default is auto.
caveats: With g-xTB the MD takes about 4 min per ps for a few dozen atoms; an MLIP is much faster.

param.nanoreactor.connect.title: Find each reaction's TS
param.nanoreactor.connect.does: Starts an ordinary TS search for each refined reaction, on its subsystem only. The barrier then lands on the reaction dot.
how: Handled by the web app, not the CLI. web/nanoreactor.py:spawn_ts_searches submits a 'ts' job on each reaction's subsystem edge as soon as the edge exists.
Smallest subsystems go first. Edges that already have a TS or channels job are skipped, up to 'Max TS searches' (20).
param.nanoreactor.connect.default: Off. 'Stop & analyze' from the interactive reactor turns it on.

param.nanoreactor.refine_live.title: Refine reactions as they appear
param.nanoreactor.refine_live.does: Refines each reaction while the MD is still running, so it reaches Explore and Analyze (and its TS search can start) before the run ends.
how: A LiveRefiner optimizes each settled event's species and subsystem ends with 'Refinement workers' (2) in parallel and writes live_network.json. The final pass reuses this work.
param.nanoreactor.refine_live.default: Off: everything is refined after the MD, leaving the CPU to the MD.

op.nanoreactor-more.title: Run longer
op.nanoreactor-more.does: Continues a finished nanoreactor's MD from its last frame with the same reactor, piston and settings. New reactions are added; earlier ones are not recomputed.
how: Reruns the original command in the same folder with --time = old time + more time, rounded up to whole piston periods.
Finished MD segments (segment_k.xyz + .mdrestart) are kept; the MD resumes after them.
The whole trajectory is analyzed again. Species and reactions refined before are reused by identity (nanoreactor.PreviousRefinement).
caveats: Not possible for a run that analyzed an external trajectory, or one that was stopped partway through a piston period.

op.complex.title: Build a complex
op.complex.does: Places several species from the graph together, unbonded, as a new complex node. It is then minimized at the workspace level.
how: Builds geometries with the chosen method (mepd.complexes.build): dock, NCI ensemble, solvation shell or packed. Screening energies are not used.
Drops any geometry whose molecules bonded or fell apart (fragment formulas must match the request) (app.py:adopt_complexes).
Adds each surviving geometry as a complex (a repeat is recognized) and queues a minimization at the workspace level.
op.complex.default: Dock (xtb aISS), keep 3, one of each.

swap.option: CREST NCI ensemble, CREST QCG shell, packed
swap.where: Method switch on the Complexes card

swap.option: Another builder (e.g. Packmol options, docking codes)

caveats: At most 12 molecules in one complex (compose.complex_members).

param.complex.method.title: How
param.complex.method.does: Chooses how the molecules are arranged.
how: dock: `xtb dock host guest --nfinal ≥3` (aISS), largest molecule first, adding one molecule at a time onto the best pose. Uses $MEPD_XTB_DOCK, else the g-xTB xtb build.
nci: start from the docked complex (packed if docking fails), then `crest --nci --T 1`. Keeps the best few; retries with --noreftopo if the topology changed.
qcg: one solute plus N copies of one solvent: `crest solute.xyz --qcg solvent.xyz --nsolv N --T 1`.
packed: random orientations in the smallest sphere (Packmol if on PATH, else the nanoreactor packer). Repacked further apart if two molecules look bonded.
param.complex.method.default: dock: seconds, and it finds H-bonds and stacking.
caveats: The xtb/CREST ranking is GFN2 level. The final order comes from the workspace-level minimization.

other.reactor.title: Interactive reactor
other.reactor.does: A live MD of the chosen molecules that you steer: drag atoms, shrink the wall, set the temperature. 'Stop & analyze' turns what happened into reactions with TS searches.
how: Packs the molecules like the nanoreactor (wall 1.15× the packing radius). A complex starts as it is, with the wall 2 Å beyond its farthest atom.
A separate process runs Langevin BAOAB (0.5 fs, friction 0.02/fs) on GFN2-xTB from tblite, in-process. Fermi smearing at 3000 K; the wavefunction is reused each step.
Drag = harmonic spring to the pointer (2–300 kcal/mol/Å², Shift ×5), force capped at 0.08 Eh/bohr. Wall: logfermi, 20 kcal/mol/Å.
Every 1.5 s, frames 2 fs apart go through the nanoreactor's event detection (events_in_frames).
Stop & analyze saves the trajectory and runs a nanoreactor job on it with TS searches on.
other.reactor.default: 800 K. Stops after 15 min unwatched; at most 2 reactors run at once.

swap.option: Other force fields/MLIPs for the live MD
swap.where: not exposed: GFN2-xTB is hard-coded in mepd/web/sandbox.py:_run (tblite Calculator)

swap.option: Unattended discovery MD at any level

caveats: Live dynamics are always GFN2-xTB, whatever the profile. Refinement and TS searches after Stop & analyze use the workspace level.
Limited element set (H–Br, I) and slider ranges: 0–5000 K, wall 3–60 Å.

other.products.title: Products
other.products.does: Shows what the chosen reactants could become together. The products you pick become reactions with both ends minimized, ready for 'Find TS'.
how: Pack the reactants (and any partner) into one complex (complexes.packed: Packmol if installed, else random packing, seed 0).
Perceive bonds (openbabel), then run the bond-rules generator: ≤ 2 breaks, ≤ 2 forms within 4.5 Å, Lewis-valid, no radicals or zwitterions, at most 40, fewest changes first.
Each product gets a 3D guess in the complex's atom order (embed_product). Products already in the graph are marked.
A picked product becomes a reaction: hidden reactant and product complexes joined by an edge, plus product species. All are queued for minimization at the workspace level.
other.products.default: Bond rules with 2 breaks / 2 forms (the propose API allows up to 3; the UI uses 2).

swap.where: 'Pick products from your graph' link: both sides are packed separately, and the TS search maps the atoms
not exposed here: mepd/web/compose.py:propose calls generators.propose('bond-rules', ...)

caveats: Which bonds can form depends on the random packing: only atom pairs within 4.5 Å in that arrangement are tried.

op.solvent.title: Solvent effects
op.solvent.does: Recomputes a finished gas-phase TS search in implicit solvents. Gives barrier, shift vs gas, half-life and the temperature for a 1 h half-life per solvent, plus insights.
how: Reads the source folder's mep_output.xyz, ts*.xyz and their IRCs (gas-phase energies at the profile's level).
Per solvent: dG_solv = E(GFN2-xTB + model) − E(GFN2-xTB gas) on each frame, two xtb runs per geometry (solvation.py:SolvationCorrection). SCC failures retry with --etemp/--iterations.
Solvent energy = E(engine) + dG_solv. Native GFN2-xTB solvent only when the engine itself is local GFN2 xtb.
Barrier = highest point along the TS's IRC minus the lowest reactant-side energy, one floor per phase.
Half-lives from Eyring with the electronic barrier (conditions.py:kinetics_row).
op.solvent.default: Six solvents (water, methanol, DMSO, acetonitrile, THF, toluene), keep gas-phase geometries, ALPB, 298.15 K. Covers protic, polar aprotic and nonpolar; single points take seconds.

swap.where: not exposed: would plug in at mepd/solvation.py:SolvationCorrection

caveats: Composite model: gas energy from your engine, solvation from GFN2-xTB. Not free energies: no thermal or entropy terms.
Refuses to run if the profile already has a [solvation] table, or if the model does not change the energy (e.g. g-xTB binary).
op.solvent.cli: mepd solvent <ts-run-folder> --solvent water --solvent dmso --mode single-point --model alpb -i profile.toml

param.solvent.mode.title: Geometries
param.solvent.mode.does: Whether the stationary points stay at their gas-phase geometries or are found again on the solvated surface.
how: Keep gas-phase: E_gas + dG_solv on every frame of the gas-phase path, TSs and IRCs. Flags when the solvated peak along an IRC moves >0.5 kcal/mol off the gas TS.
Re-optimize: single points first (kept in single-point/), then the engine is wrapped in the solvent (solvate_engine).
Path ends re-minimized with the profile's geometry optimizer.
Each TS re-optimized from the solvated IRC peak, then from the gas TS; accepted only if its IRC ends have the same bonds as the gas IRC ends.
param.solvent.mode.default: Keep gas-phase: seconds, and fair while the solvent does not move the TS much.
caveats: For charged or strongly polar TSs, single points can be off: confirm with Re-optimize.

param.solvent.model.title: Solvent model
param.solvent.model.does: Which GFN2-xTB implicit solvent model gives the solvation free energy.
how: Passed to xtb as --alpb, --gbsa or --cpcmx with the solvent name (solvation.py:SolvationCorrection).
Same flags for the gas/solvent pair on every frame, so dG_solv is a clean difference.
param.solvent.model.default: ALPB: parametrized for all 17 listed solvents.

swap.where: this field (--model gbsa); not for octanol, nitromethane, ethyl acetate, dioxane

caveats: Needs an xtb binary that runs GFN2-xTB; the g-xTB-only gxtb binary has no solvent model.

op.mechanochem.title: Mechanical force
op.mechanochem.does: Ranks atom pairs to pull apart that speed up or slow down each channel, the force for a 1 h half-life, and forces at which a slower channel overtakes the fastest.
how: Loads each channel's reactant, TS and product from a ts/tsopt/channels result (cli_force.py:load_channels).
For every heavy-atom pair: dq = d(TS) − d(reactant). Bell: ΔE‡(F) = ΔE‡(0) − F·dq; 1 nN·Å = 14.39 kcal/mol (mechanochem.py:analyze).
Levers need |dq| > 0.05 Å; top 5 per direction. Crossovers scanned up to the largest force.
Check under force: ForcedEngine adds −F·d_ij (EFEI); reactant minimized, TS + IRC re-optimized at each force for the main levers.
op.mechanochem.default: Estimate (Bell, instant), heavy atoms only, scan to 2.5 nN, 298.15 K.

swap.where: not exposed: would plug in at mepd/mechanochem.py:analyze

caveats: Off in the web UI for now; `mepd force` runs it on the command line.
Bell is first order: trusted to ~1 nN. Does not say which atoms can carry a handle.

param.mechanochem.mode.title: Method
param.mechanochem.mode.does: First-order estimate from existing geometries, or barriers recomputed on the force-modified surface.
how: Estimate: Bell's ΔE‡ − F·dq from the reactant–TS distance change of each pair.
Check under force: ForcedEngine (E − F·Σd_ij) around the profile's engine; reactant minimized, TS optimized and IRC run at each force (default 0.5, 1, 1.5 nN).
Done for the fastest channel's strongest lever and the leading selectivity switch; IRC must connect the same minima.
caveats: Mechanical force is off in the web UI.

op.substituents.title: Substituent effects
op.substituents.does: Replaces one hydrogen at a time with functional groups and reports each barrier shift, a Hammett slope per site, and groups that change which channel wins.
how: Sites: H bonded to the same heavy atom at both IRC ends; symmetry-equivalent H merged (Weisfeiler–Lehman ranks). Closest to the reacting atoms first.
Group built once in 3D with RDKit (ETKDG embed, MMFF94), placed along the old X–H bond at covalent length, spun to avoid clashes (substituents.py:attach).
Same group added to reactant end, TS and product end in the same atom order.
Fast: only new atoms relaxed (ASE LBFGS on the profile's engine), single points; parent gets the same protocol.
Shift = barrier(variant) − barrier(parent); slope by least squares vs Hammett σp (≥4 groups).
op.substituents.default: NH2, OH, OMe, Me, F, Cl, CF3, CN, NO2 (donor to acceptor), fast mode, up to 8 sites.
caveats: Fast shifts: TS is no longer a saddle; re-optimize before trusting shifts ≥8 kcal/mol.
σp is a para-aryl scale; elsewhere a rough donor/acceptor ranking.
Variants where the group forms/breaks bonds or clashes (<1.2 Å) are flagged.

param.substituents.mode.title: Geometries
param.substituents.mode.does: Whether only the new group relaxes, or each variant's TS and reactant are optimized again.
how: Fast: new group atoms minimized with the rest fixed (ASE FixAtoms + LBFGS, fmax 0.05, ≤300 steps), then single points of reactant, TS, product.
Re-optimize: reactant minimized, TS optimized, IRC run; status other_minima if the IRC ends lack the substituted ends' bonds.
Parent goes through the same protocol so shifts compare like with like.
param.substituents.mode.default: Fast: seconds per variant. Checked on Menshutkin: within ~2 kcal/mol of re-optimized shifts.

swap.option: Re-optimize the TS (about a minute each)

param.substituents.groups.title: Groups
param.substituents.groups.does: Which functional groups replace the hydrogen at each site.
how: Each group's SMILES comes from Design's group list (web/design.py:GROUPS).
Embedded with RDKit (seed 7) and MMFF94-optimized once, then cached.
Labels show Hammett σp (Hansch, Leo, Taft 1991) where known.
param.substituents.groups.default: NH2, OH, OMe, Me, F, Cl, CF3, CN, NO2: strong donor to strong acceptor, small enough to be quick.

op.variant-fast.title: Network variant: fast estimate
op.variant-fast.does: Estimates a network variant reaction's barrier and reaction-energy shift against its parent, with the edit built into the parent's geometries.
how: Variant spec (JSON) written when the variant is made: edit carried through the network by graph matching (network_variants.py:propagate, apply_edit).
New atoms relaxed with everything else fixed (substituents.relax_group, ASE LBFGS on the profile's engine).
Single points on reactant, TS, product; shifts vs parent energies at the same level.
Status 'reacted' if the new atoms formed or broke bonds.
When done, the re-optimization is queued automatically (web/variants.py:after_job).
caveats: The TS is not a saddle of the new molecule: a first estimate.
op.variant-fast.cli: mepd variant variant.json --mode fast -i profile.toml -o out

op.variant-reopt.title: Network variant: re-optimize
op.variant-reopt.does: Gives the variant reaction a verified TS: ends minimized, TS optimized from the substituted guess, IRC checked against the ends.
how: Starts from the fast estimate's frames when it succeeded.
Both ends minimized with the profile's optimizer; flagged ends_changed if bonds or tetrahedral configurations change.
TS optimized and IRC run (cli_common._optimize_ts_and_irc); verified if the IRC ends have the substituted ends' bonds.
Barrier from the lower of the minimized end and IRC end. Minimized ends become the edge's conformers.
If no verified TS: the parent's own path search (ts or channels) is queued on the variant's ends.
op.variant-reopt.cli: mepd variant variant.json --mode reoptimize -i profile.toml -o out

op.qmmm-build.title: Put in explicit solvent (QM/MM)
op.qmmm-build.does: Makes a new QM/MM system: the molecule (QM) inside a droplet of explicit solvent molecules (environment). Every later job on it runs embedded.
how: Solvent molecules placed at random orientations at the liquid's number density, ≥2.1 Å from any atom, out to the shell thickness (qmmm_build.py:solvate).
Shell relaxed with GFN-FF (xtb), molecule held fixed (relax_environment).
Region: molecule = QM atoms; environment beyond the moving-shell radius frozen (QMMMRegion.build).
Result added as a QM/MM node and minimized at the workspace level, with [qmmm] added to the profile.
op.qmmm-build.default: Water, 6 Å shell, 5 Å moving shell, GFN-FF environment (mechanical embedding: any QM level).

swap.option: AMBER via OpenMM, TeraChem QM/MM, your own region on an XYZ/PDB

swap.where: not exposed: would plug in at mepd/qmmm_build.py:solvate

caveats: The droplet is a starting structure, not an equilibrated liquid.
A TS cannot be embedded here: find it again inside the solvent.
op.qmmm-build.cli: mepd qmmm build mol.xyz --solvent water --shell 6 --active-radius 5 --mm gfnff

param.qmmm-build.mm.title: Environment level
param.qmmm-build.mm.does: How the solvent is computed and how it acts on the QM region.
how: GFN-FF / GFN2-xTB / GFN1-xTB: subtractive ONIOM, E = E_QM(model) + E_low(real) − E_low(model), low level via xtb (engines/qmmm.py:_XTBLow).
Model = QM atoms capped with link hydrogens on cut bonds.
TIP3P: additive, OpenMM with TIP3P charges (flexible), QM atoms get UFF Lennard-Jones; QM feels the point charges (electrostatic embedding, tip3p_system).
OpenMM environments use microiterations: the environment relaxed with force-field steps between QM steps.
param.qmmm-build.mm.default: GFN-FF: no parameters needed, any element, works with any QM level (mechanical embedding).

swap.where: this field; needs a point-charge QM level (engine xtb, psi4 or terachem)

caveats: Mechanical embedding: the QM electrons are not polarized by the solvent.
TIP3P needs every environment molecule to be water.

param.qmmm-build.active_radius.title: Moving shell (Å)
param.qmmm-build.active_radius.does: Environment atoms within this distance of the QM region move in optimizations, path searches, TS searches and IRCs; the rest is frozen.
how: Whole small molecules are taken in or out at a time (qmmm.py:active_shell).
Frozen atoms are held by FrozenAtomsEngine and left out of Hessians.

swap.option: Freeze the whole environment along a path (cage) or mean-force path
