profile.path_method.title: Path method
profile.path_method.does: Picks the algorithm that relaxes the path between two minima. Every method runs inside the same recursive driver (MSMEP), which splits a path at intermediates and searches each piece again.
how: MSMEP builds the initial path (Initial path choice), then hands it to the path minimizer chosen here (mepd/msmep.py:_construct_path_minimizer).

NEB: mepd's own nudged elastic band, images moved by the Chain optimizer. FSM (FNEB): freezing string grown from both ends. FSM + TS check: FSM, Sella/geomeTRIC TS optimization from the highest image, then a pseudo-IRC.
GSM: the compiled molecularGSM binary, which calls back into this profile's engine per node through a generated grad.py.
MLP-GI: minimizes the path's energy-weighted geodesic length with two FIRE stages (mepd/mlp_geodesic.py). geomeTRIC NEB: geometric.neb. DL-FIND NEB: TeraChem's DL-FIND via QCCompute/ChemCloud.
Unless switched off, the converged path is checked for being one elementary step; if not, it is split and each piece searched again.
profile.path_method.default: NEB (RunInputs.path_min_method). It needs no external binary and works with every engine.

profile.engine.title: Engine
profile.engine.does: Sets where every energy, gradient, Hessian, minimization and TS optimization of a calculation comes from: the level of theory.

xTB: XTBEngine runs xtb with GFN2 or GFN1. Psi4: a worker in Psi4's own Python. TeraChem: one terachem run per gradient, previous orbitals as guess.
QCCompute/ChemCloud: QCComputeEngine sends qcdata ProgramInputs to the chosen Program locally (qccompute) or remotely (chemcloud); minimizations and TS searches go through geomeTRIC.
MLIP, FAIR-Chem, ASE: an ASE calculator wrapped by ASEEngine or FAIRChemEngine; minimizations use the ASE optimizer set in Advanced, TS searches and IRCs use Sella.
Optional wrappers applied after: implicit solvent (SolvatedEngine), QM/MM embedding, frozen atoms.

profile.solvent.does: Puts every calculation at this level in an implicit solvent. Energies, gradients, minimizations, TS searches and IRCs all run on the solvated surface.

Native: when the engine is the g-xTB engine running GFN2 (add_gxtb_flag = false, executable not the gxtb-only binary), --alpb <solvent> is passed to xtb.
Every other engine (g-xTB, MLIPs, ASE, DFT): SolvatedEngine adds E_GFN2+ALPB(x) − E_GFN2(x) and its gradient, from two GFN2-xTB runs per geometry.

profile.interpolation.title: Initial path
profile.interpolation.does: How the first guess path between two structures is built, and every sub-path a recursive split creates.
how: Geodesic: run_geodesic in mepd/geodesic_interpolation2 (Zhu, Thompson, Martínez 2019): a path in redundant internal coordinates, tuned by friction, nudge and random seed.
LST: each image independently fits linearly interpolated interatomic distances (weights 1/d⁴), starting from the linear image.
IDPP: the same target distances, all images relaxed together as an NEB on that pair surface, so they stay evenly spaced.
Linear: straight Cartesian lines after Kabsch alignment of the end onto the start.
Frozen atoms follow the linear path in every method. GSM, when seeded, starts from this path; FSM grows its own and only uses alignment.
profile.interpolation.default: Geodesic (ChainInputs.interpolation): keeps bonds sensible, which avoids atoms passing through each other.

profile.optimizer.title: Chain optimizer
profile.optimizer.does: How NEB and FSM move the path's images each step from their projected forces.
how: RunInputs builds the optimizer from [optimizer_kwds] name; NEB/FSM call its optimize_step with the chain's NEB gradient each step.
Conjugate gradient: Polak–Ribière+ directions, step capped by max_step_norm, time step adapted from gradient correlation between steps.

L-BFGS: inverse-Hessian estimate from the last 10 steps. FIRE: Bitzek et al. 2006 velocity mixing. Velocity-projected, adaptive momentum (Adam-like with step caps), Adam, SGD, gradient descent also available.
Each optimizer's own settings appear under Advanced once picked.
profile.optimizer.default: Conjugate gradient (RunInputs sets name = "cg" when none is given).

profile.gi_inputs.nimages.title: Images
profile.gi_inputs.nimages.does: How many structures the initial path has, ends included.
how: Every initial path and split sub-path is built with this many images (mepd/interpolation.py:initial_chain).
NEB optimizes them; with Adaptive resolution it may add more up to Adaptive max images.
GSM seeded from the initial path uses this as its node count (Nodes is then ignored). MLP-GI starts with these and adds images near barriers.
caveats: Too few images can miss a barrier between two images; the TS check later refines it.

profile.path_min_inputs.climb.title: Climb
profile.path_min_inputs.climb.does: Turns on a climbing image so the path's top image converges onto the saddle point. The meaning differs per method.
how: NEB: after the band converges and the elementary-step check passes, a new image is inserted between the highest image and its higher neighbour. Only that image climbs, up to 100 steps, until its max |g_perp| ≤ TS gradient threshold (NEB._run_post_convergence_climbing_refinement).
MLP-GI: in stage 2 the highest node's gradient along the tangent is inverted, scaled by Climbing strength (alpha_climb, default 0.5).
geomeTRIC NEB: a number passed to geometric.neb as its climb parameter; true means 0.5, false 0.
profile.path_min_inputs.climb.default: On for NEB and MLP-GI; 0.5 for geomeTRIC NEB.
caveats: NEB only climbs paths judged elementary; a multi-step path is split first.

profile.path_min_inputs.adaptive_resolut.title: Adaptive resolution
profile.path_min_inputs.adaptive_resolut.does: NEB adds images where the band is hardest to converge instead of starting with more.
how: Each step NEB checks whether convergence has plateaued and the only unmet criterion is the largest image RMS perpendicular gradient.
If so, it inserts one image in the segment around the image with the largest RMS g_perp (NEB._maybe_adapt_chain_resolution).
Limited by Adaptive max images (default 20) and a cooldown between insertions.

profile.path_min_inputs.do_elem_step_che.title: Do elem step checks
profile.path_min_inputs.do_elem_step_che.does: Decides whether a converged path is a single elementary step; if not, MSMEP splits it at the minima found and searches each piece.
how: Intermediate minima along the path are minimized; any that are new species split the path there (minima split).
Otherwise a pseudo-IRC: the images flanking the highest one (upsampled if the peak is next to an end) are minimized and compared with the ends by bond graph, RMSD and energy.
Neither end found: split at the new structures (maxima split).

profile.path_min_inputs.use_geodesic_tan.title: Use geodesic tangent
profile.path_min_inputs.use_geodesic_tan.does: NEB uses the geodesic path's tangent at each image instead of the tangent from neighbouring image differences.
how: Passed as geodesic_tangent to mepd/chainhelpers.py:compute_NEB_gradient, which projects forces with that tangent.

profile.path_min_inputs.pseudo_irc_hessi.title: Pseudo IRC hessian
profile.path_min_inputs.pseudo_irc_hessi.does: FSM + TS check: where the Hessian at the optimized TS comes from. It gives the imaginary mode the TS is pushed along and counts imaginary frequencies.
how: auto: central differences of the engine's gradients (GradientHessianEngine, 6N gradient calls) when the engine is g-xTB, the engine's own Hessian otherwise.
engine: the engine's compute_hessian (g-xTB: xtb --hess; QCCompute: the program's Hessian).
gradients: always central differences of gradients.
Modes are projected (rigid-body motion removed) in vri.stationary_point_modes; frequencies below −cutoff (20 cm⁻¹) count as imaginary.
profile.path_min_inputs.pseudo_irc_hessi.default: auto. g-xTB's own Hessian disagrees with its gradients by up to ~0.02 Eh/bohr², which can flip soft modes.

profile.path_min_inputs.fallback.title: Fallback
profile.path_min_inputs.fallback.does: FSM + TS check: what searches the pair when the TS does not join it.
how: Triggered when the TS optimization fails, ends at a minimum or a higher-order saddle, both pseudo-IRC sides minimize to the same end, or a side leads back to a species from a pair split above.
GSM: molecularGSM with its own elementary-step check (Fallback settings: gsm_inputs). If no GSM binary, or GSM fails, NEB runs instead.
NEB: mepd's NEB with neb_inputs overrides. none: keep the FSM path and run the usual elementary-step check on [start, highest image, end].
profile.path_min_inputs.fallback.default: GSM: on 20 KAIST reactions it found the lowest channel more often than NEB (17 vs 14 within 1 kcal/mol of the best method).

swap.where: this field; settings in gsm_inputs / neb_inputs

profile.path_min_inputs.tangent.title: Tangent
profile.path_min_inputs.tangent.does: FSM: the direction new images are grown along from each frontier.
how: geodesic: the tangent of a geodesic interpolation between the two frontier images.
linear: the straight Cartesian difference between them.

profile.path_min_inputs.distance_metric.title: Distance metric
profile.path_min_inputs.distance_metric.does: FSM: how the gap between the two growing frontiers is measured, which sets growth step size and when the string has joined.
how: GEODESIC: length along a geodesic interpolation. RMSD: aligned RMSD between images. LINEAR: Cartesian distance (FreezingNEB._distance_function).

profile.path_min_inputs.seed_with_geodes.title: Seed with geodesic interpolation
profile.path_min_inputs.seed_with_geodes.does: GSM starts from mepd's initial path (built with the Initial path choice) instead of growing its own string from the two ends.
how: The initial path is written as restart.xyz0000 and molecularGSM's RESTART mechanism reads it, skipping its internal-coordinate growth (GSM._build_geodesic_seed).
The string then has Images nodes; Nodes is ignored.
Off: GSM grows the string from the ends in its own internal coordinates up to Nodes.

profile.path_min_inputs.early_stop_on_mi.title: Early stop on minima
profile.path_min_inputs.early_stop_on_mi.does: Stops GSM when the string develops a stable intermediate minimum, so MSMEP can split there instead of GSM running to its iteration limit.
how: After growth, the live string is read each GSM iteration (from mepd's patched binary output).
A local minimum that holds for 10 iterations (early_stop_persistence_window), never before iteration 20, stops the run.
The stop is verified by the elementary-step check; if the path turns out elementary, GSM resumes to full convergence.
Only active when Do elem step checks is on.

profile.path_min_inputs.ts_final_type.title: TS final type
profile.path_min_inputs.ts_final_type.does: Tells molecularGSM what kind of TS to expect: 1 if a bond breaks, 0 otherwise. GSM uses it to judge when the string has found the TS.
how: Written to molecularGSM's input deck (TS_FINAL_TYPE) by mepd/pathminimizers/gsm.py:_inpfileq_text.

profile.path_min_inputs.mlp_model.title: Optimize on
profile.path_min_inputs.mlp_model.does: MLP-GI: the surface the geodesic path is optimized on. The final path is always re-scored on this profile's engine.
how: Empty: the profile's engine evaluates every node and midpoint.
A model name: build_mlip_engine loads that machine-learned potential as a surrogate (Model device, Model checkpoint); the optimized path's energies are then recomputed with the profile's engine.
caveats: A surrogate's path may not be the minimum-energy path on the profile's own surface; the TS check afterwards decides.

profile.chain_inputs.k.title: Spring constant k
profile.chain_inputs.k.does: Maximum spring constant between NEB images; with Spring spread Δk, springs are energy-weighted so images bunch near the barrier.
how: Per segment: k = (1−α)·k + α·(k−Δk), α = (E_max − E_i)/(E_max − E_ref), E_ref = higher of the two ends, E_i = higher of the segment's two images.
Segments below E_ref get k−Δk (chainhelpers._k_between_nodes).

profile.chain_inputs.delta_k.title: Spring spread Δk
profile.chain_inputs.delta_k.does: Maximum spring constant between NEB images; with Spring spread Δk, springs are energy-weighted so images bunch near the barrier.
how: Per segment: k = (1−α)·k + α·(k−Δk), α = (E_max − E_i)/(E_max − E_ref), E_ref = higher of the two ends, E_i = higher of the segment's two images.
Segments below E_ref get k−Δk (chainhelpers._k_between_nodes).

profile.chain_inputs.node_freezing.title: Node freezing
profile.chain_inputs.node_freezing.does: NEB stops computing images that have converged, saving engine calls.
how: An image is frozen once its own gradient is below the convergence thresholds times Fraction freeze (default 0.1).

profile.gxtb_engine_kwds.hessian_acc.title: Hessian accuracy
profile.gxtb_engine_kwds.hessian_acc.does: SCC accuracy (xtb --acc) for g-xTB's numerical Hessians. Smaller is tighter.
how: Passed to gxtb --hess runs. At xtb's default 1.0 Hessian elements are off by ~0.01–0.03 Eh/bohr²; 0.001 matches central differences of g-xTB gradients to ~1e-4 for ~20% more time.
caveats: Even tight, g-xTB's --hess is not fully consistent with its gradients; FSM + TS check uses gradient differences by default.

profile.xtb_engine_kwds.method.title: Method
profile.xtb_engine_kwds.method.does: For the xTB engine: GFN2-xTB or GFN1-xTB.
how: XTBEngine runs the xtb program with that Hamiltonian, with point-charge support for electrostatic QM/MM.

profile.fairchem_engine_kwds.task.title: Task
profile.fairchem_engine_kwds.task.does: Which UMA output head the FAIR-Chem model uses.
how: Passed to FAIRChemEngine; omol is the molecular head and reads charge and multiplicity.

swap.where: this field (materials, catalysis, MOF, crystal heads)

profile.fairchem_engine_kwds.inference_s.title: Inference settings
profile.fairchem_engine_kwds.inference_s.does: Speed vs startup trade-off of the FAIR-Chem model.
how: default: uncompiled, no activation checkpointing; ready in seconds, any molecules.
compile: torch.compile, ~2.5× faster per call, but 20–40 s compile per process and one molecule only.
turbo: compile plus TF32 (some accuracy for speed).

profile.ase_engine_kwds.geometry_optimiz.title: Geometry optimizer
profile.ase_engine_kwds.geometry_optimiz.does: The ASE optimizer used for minimizations with this engine. TS optimizations and IRCs use Sella regardless.
how: ASEEngine runs the ASE optimizer of that name (ase.optimize) for each minimization with the engine's calculator.

profile.mlip_engine_kwds.geometry_optimi.title: Geometry optimizer
profile.mlip_engine_kwds.geometry_optimi.does: The ASE optimizer used for minimizations with this engine. TS optimizations and IRCs use Sella regardless.
how: ASEEngine runs the ASE optimizer of that name (ase.optimize) for each minimization with the engine's calculator.

profile.fairchem_engine_kwds.geometry_op.title: Geometry optimizer
profile.fairchem_engine_kwds.geometry_op.does: The ASE optimizer used for minimizations with this engine. TS optimizations and IRCs use Sella regardless.
how: ASEEngine runs the ASE optimizer of that name (ase.optimize) for each minimization with the engine's calculator.

profile.geometry_optimizer_kwds.coordsys.title: Coordsys
profile.geometry_optimizer_kwds.coordsys.does: Coordinate system geomeTRIC uses for QCCompute/ChemCloud minimizations and TS optimizations.
how: Passed as a geomeTRIC keyword in the ProgramInput whose program is geometric and subprogram the chosen Program.

profile.atom_mapping_inputs.metric.title: Metric
profile.atom_mapping_inputs.metric.does: How candidate atom mappings (and, in channels, conformer pairs) are compared when atom mapping is on.
how: Candidates come from SLAPMapper (sequential linear-assignment mapping), plus symmetric relabelings and 'don't reindex'.

Snap + GI + xtb: snap's lowest-RMSD relabelings, each interpolated (geodesic), scored by GFN2-xTB energy along the path; lowest peak wins. Without xtb: shortest interpolation; without interpolation: lowest RMSD.
Endpoint RMSD: aligned RMSD of the two ends (fast, weakest). GI path: geodesic path length (slower). Filtered GI path: GI only for pairs within rmsd_window standard deviations of the lowest RMSD.
caveats: Scoring uses GFN2-xTB from an installed xtb (no download), whatever the profile's engine.

profile.atom_mapping_inputs.relax_top.title: Relax top
profile.atom_mapping_inputs.relax_top.does: Snap + GI + xtb: re-ranks the best mappings by a relaxed path energy instead of the raw interpolation peak.
how: The N best by raw xtb peak, plus SLAPMapper's minimal mapping, have their paths relaxed with the changing bonds held (_relaxed_barrier).
Lowest relaxed barrier wins; a mapping with more bond changes than SLAPMapper's must beat it by Relax margin (5 kcal/mol).
profile.atom_mapping_inputs.relax_top.default: 4. Raw interpolation peaks are mostly atoms colliding mid-path. 0 = raw peaks only.

profile.atom_mapping_inputs.explore_mech.title: Explore mechanisms
profile.atom_mapping_inputs.explore_mech.does: Also considers up to this many mechanisms beyond SLAPMapper's minimal-edit ones: relays and exchanges through other molecules.
how: explore_mechanisms swaps images of same-element atoms or groups, keeping swaps that raise the bond-edit count by at most 2 per round (5 rounds).
Each new route is scored like SLAPMapper's (snap + GI + xtb) and, in channels, searched as its own mechanism; catalytic ones are labelled.

profile.qmmm_environment.title: Environment along a path
profile.qmmm_environment.does: For QM/MM systems: what the MM environment does while a path is searched. Ignored without [qmmm].
how: Relaxed: the moving shell (within active_radius of the QM region) is optimized with each structure; the outer shell is frozen.
Cage: everything but the QM atoms frozen; the path is found in the fixed field.

Free energy (mean_force): MeanForceEngine replaces each gradient with its mean over MD of the environment (xtb dynamics at the low level, or OpenMM for AMBER/TIP3P) with the solute held; the barrier comes from thermodynamic integration along the path.

swap.option: cage, mean_force (Temperature, Equilibration, Sampling, Frames, Restraint, Time step)

caveats: Free energy is much slower: each geometry needs an MD run (defaults 300 K, 0.5 ps equilibration, 1 ps sampling, 10 frames).

kinetics.model.title: Kinetics
kinetics.model.does: Turns the workspace network into a mass-action microkinetic model and integrates amounts over time from the starting mixture.
how: build(): species = structures with an energy at the workspace level; each reaction or edge becomes a reversible Step with the lowest TS energy (not a barrier) from finished TS searches at that level. Duplicate channels keep only their lowest TS.
A complex counts as its separated molecules: reactions run from separated reactants to separated products; edges touching a complex are skipped.

Rates (microkinetics.Network.rate_constants): k = (k_BT/h)·exp(−(G_top − ΣG_side)/RT), G_top = max(G_TS, ΣG_reactants, ΣG_products), units M^(1−n) s⁻¹, 1 M standard state. Forward and reverse share the TS, so detailed balance holds.
simulate(): scipy solve_ivp, Radau, analytic Jacobian, rtol 1e-8, atol 1e-14 M; output on log- and linear-spaced times. Steady = nothing changes by >0.1% over the run.
caveats: A TS below one of its sides counts as barrierless that way (warned).
Bimolecular steps use the same k_BT/h prefactor; with electronic energies they lack the entropy cost of meeting, so absolute rates are orders of magnitude off. Read ratios and trends.
One structure per species; no conformer averaging, no diffusion limit.

swap.option: Free energies instead of electronic energies

kinetics.free_energy.title: free energies
kinetics.free_energy.does: Replaces each species' and TS's electronic energy with G(T) = E + quasi-RRHO correction, so entropy (association costs, soft modes) enters the rates.
how: GFN2-xTB single-point Hessian at each stored geometry (xtb --bhess, in the level profile's implicit solvent if any), computed once per structure and cached in the workspace's thermo/ folder.
TS geometries: ts*.xyz in the TS search's output (and its 'Sample more paths' runs) whose energy matches within 2 mEh. None found: the reactant side's correction is used.

thermo.qrrho: ZPE, harmonic vibrations, rigid rotor, Sackur-Tetrode translation at 1 mol/L, R ln(multiplicity). Modes below ~50 cm⁻¹ blend toward free-rotor entropy (Grimme 2012). The TS's imaginary mode is dropped.
Recomputed at every temperature of a sweep from the same frequencies; two xtb runs at a time, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.
kinetics.free_energy.default: On in the UI. Without it, complexes look too stable.

swap.option: Frequencies from the level's own engine or another program

caveats: Energies E stay at the workspace level (e.g. g-xTB); only the thermal correction is GFN2-xTB.
Association entropy uses gas-phase formulas, which overstate it in solution. One conformer per species.
Structures with extra imaginary modes below −20 cm⁻¹ are listed in the warnings.

kinetics.include_unverified.title: include unverified barriers
kinetics.include_unverified.does: Lets steps whose barrier is only a path maximum (no TS/IRC confirmation) into the model. Without it those steps are left out.
how: edge_ts() collects TS energies at the workspace level from finished TS-search jobs on the edge; a job counts as verified unless its summary says barrier_verified = false. Barriers recorded on the edge's origin count as verified.
The lowest verified TS is used if any; else, with this on, the lowest unverified one.
Unverified steps are marked ≈ in 'Where the material went'.
kinetics.include_unverified.default: On in the UI (the API default is off).
caveats: A path maximum is an upper bound on the TS energy, so those steps can look slower than they are.

kinetics.temperature.title: Temperature
kinetics.temperature.does: Sets T in every rate constant (k_BT/h and RT in the exponent) and, with free energies, the T of the thermal corrections.
how: Passed to microkinetics.simulate and, with free energies on, to energies_at(T) before the run.

kinetics.time.title: Time
kinetics.time.does: How long the flask runs. Sets the end amounts and the point where 'amount at the end' and degree of control are measured.
how: Integration from 0 to this time; output on 79 log-spaced points from min(1e-12 s, 1e-6·time) plus 41 evenly spaced ones.
caveats: If the run is already at equilibrium by then, no barrier controls the result; use a shorter time or lower T to see kinetic control.

kinetics.held.title: fixed
kinetics.held.does: Holds a starting species at its amount throughout (a constant feed, chemostat). With any fixed species the run heads to a steady state instead of equilibrium.
how: Held species get dc/dt = 0 in the ODE (the 'free' mask in microkinetics.simulate); they still react.

kinetics.target.title: Target
kinetics.target.does: Picks one species to report: its end amount, its formation rate, and which TSs and species control it.
how: Formation rate = net stoichiometry · net step rates at the end (formation_rate).
Degree of rate control (Campbell): each TS energy shifted ±0.2 kcal/mol, the model re-run, X = d ln Q / d(−G/RT) by central differences. Same for each species (thermodynamic degree of control).
Bars show the factor exp(X/RT) per 1 kcal/mol lower.
caveats: Costs two extra simulations per step and per species.

kinetics.control_what.title: amount at the end / formation rate
kinetics.control_what.does: Which quantity Q the degree of control is computed for: the target's amount at the end, or its net formation rate at the end.
how: Passed as what= to microkinetics.degree_of_control; _quantity returns c[end, target] or formation_rate.
caveats: In a closed flask the end rate goes to zero at equilibrium; with a feed it is the steady-state rate.

kinetics.sweep.title: temperature sweep
kinetics.sweep.does: Re-runs the model at 9 temperatures between the two bounds and shows end amounts against T, plus the target's speed-up and apparent activation energy.
how: The UI sends 9 evenly spaced temperatures (the server takes at most 12).
microkinetics.sweep runs simulate at each; with free energies, energies_at(T) recomputes every G(T) from the cached frequencies.
Apparent Ea from the Arrhenius slope of the target's formation rate between neighbouring temperatures.
caveats: Without free energies only k_BT/h and RT change with T; species energies stay fixed.

kinetics.compare.title: compare with parent
kinetics.compare.does: Runs a network variant and its parent (or the variant it is built on) from the same mixture, side by side.
how: compare_inputs maps the mixture onto the variant: amounts of a replaced species go to its variant.
analyze() runs on each network; variant steps without a re-optimized TS yet use a fast estimate (the parent's barrier shifted by the edit), marked est.

other.surroundings.title: Surroundings
other.surroundings.does: Where the selection is modelled. Molecule, reaction and network tools all run in whichever surroundings the selection is in.
how: Gas phase: the molecules alone, at the workspace level of theory.

Solvent (implicit): Explore › Conditions picks a solvent for the whole network. Each barrier shows its value in that solvent once a 'Solvent effects' run has recomputed it (GFN2-xTB + ALPB/CPCM-X correction on the gas-phase path, solvation.py:SolvationCorrection); until then the gas value, marked 'gas'.

Explicit: a QM/MM system, the molecule (QM) in a droplet of solvent molecules (GFN-FF environment by default, qmmm_build.py:solvate). It is its own node in the graph; jobs on it run embedded (QMMMEngine).
Protein: a QM/MM system in a protein pocket: dock with AutoDock Vina, pick a site, build the system (AMBER/OpenMM environment, qmmm_protein.py).
A species already modelled somewhere else (same SMILES and charge) is offered as 'go to it' instead of building again.

swap.option: A different implicit model or solvent
swap.where: Explore › Conditions (setup solvent), or a barrier job's 'Solvent effects' follow-up

swap.option: Environment level for explicit solvent (TIP3P, GFN2-xTB, GFN1-xTB)
Your own QM/MM system (PDB/prmtop, TeraChem input)
swap.where: the add box's 'QM/MM system…' (Playground layout › Add), then select it

caveats: Implicit solvent corrects energies along gas-phase geometries; it does not re-optimize them in solvent.
Explicit and protein systems are separate nodes: a reaction found in one stays in it.
